headline: Sertraline versus placebo for late-life depression in primary care: a 12-week randomized controlled trial
subtitle: Ensaio clínico randomizado · Journal of Affective Disorders · 2024
one_sentence_summary: Sertraline is superior to placebo for late-life depression treated in primary care and is well tolerated.
reference: Ana Beatriz Moreira, Carlos Eduardo Lima, Fernanda Ribeiro Santos, João Pedro Almeida. Sertraline versus placebo for late-life depression in primary care: a 12-week randomized controlled trial. Journal of Affective Disorders. 2024. doi:10.1016/j.jad.2024.00001

study_design.population: Participants were adults aged 65 years or older with a diagnosis of major depressive disorder and a baseline HAM-D score of at least 14.
study_design.intervention: Patients received sertraline 50 mg daily, titrated to 100 mg at week 4 if tolerated, or matching placebo.
study_design.comparator: We conducted a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial in 14 primary care units of a public health network.
study_design.outcomes: The primary outcome was the change in HAM-D score from baseline to week 12.
study_design.follow_up: Follow-up visits occurred at weeks 4, 8 and 12.

flow.label: Pergunta
flow.detail: We aimed to determine whether sertraline is superior to placebo over 12 weeks.

flow.label: Intervenção / Análise
flow.detail: Patients received sertraline 50 mg daily, titrated to 100 mg at week 4 if tolerated, or matching placebo.

flow.label: Resultados
flow.detail: At week 12, HAM-D scores fell by 9.8 ± 5.2 points with sertraline and 5.7 ± 5.4 points with placebo (mean difference −4.1, 95% CI −5.6 to −2.6; p < 0.001).

flow.label: Conclusão
flow.detail: Sertraline is superior to placebo for late-life depression treated in primary care and is well tolerated.

key_findings.detail: Response was achieved by 58% of the sertraline group and 34% of the placebo group (OR = 2.7, 95% CI 1.6 to 4.5; p < 0.001).

key_findings.title: Discontinuation due to adverse events was 6% with sertraline…
key_findings.detail: Discontinuation due to adverse events was 6% with sertraline and 4% with placebo (p = 0.42).

takeaways: Sertraline is superior to placebo for late-life depression treated in primary care and is well tolerated.
Longer trials should evaluate relapse prevention and outcomes in patients with cognitive impairment.
clinical_implications: Sertraline produced a clinically meaningful reduction in depressive symptoms compared with placebo in older primary care patients.
In clinical practice, the results support sertraline as a first-line option for late-life depression when psychotherapy is unavailable.
limitations: Limitations include the exclusion of patients with dementia, which limits generalizability, and the relatively short 12-week follow-up.
